renewables.solar_declination.title: Solar declination angle (Cooper)
assumptions: Cooper approximation; declination ranges ±23.45° (solstices), 0 at the equinoxes. Inverting δ → n is two-valued: a given declination occurs on two days of the year, and the solver returns the root closest in log-distance to the example n (for δ = 0 with the example n = 172 that is n ≈ 263.5, the September equinox).

renewables.solar_hour_angle.title: Solar hour angle from clock (solar) time

variables.name: h
variables.desc: solar time of day in hours as a number (noon = 12)

assumptions: Solar time, not clock time: 15° of hour angle per hour (ω = 15°(h − 12)).

renewables.solar_incidence.title: Solar incidence angle on a tilted surface

variables.name: theta
variables.desc: incidence angle between beam and surface normal
variables.label: θ

variables.name: gamma
variables.desc: surface azimuth from due SOUTH, west positive (γ = 0 faces the equator only in the northern hemisphere; use γ = 180° for equator-facing south of the equator)
variables.label: γ

assumptions: Duffie–Beckman convention: γ = 0 when the surface faces the equator (south in the northern hemisphere) and is positive toward the west. For a horizontal surface (β = 0) this reduces to the zenith angle cos θ_z = sin δ sin φ + cos δ cos φ cos ω.
method_references: Duffie & Beckman, Solar Engineering of Thermal Processes, incidence-angle relation (recalled)

renewables.tilted_irradiance.title: Irradiance on a tilted surface (isotropic-sky Liu–Jordan)

variables.name: gamma
variables.desc: surface azimuth from due SOUTH, west positive (γ = 0 faces the equator only in the northern hemisphere; use γ = 180° for equator-facing south of the equator)
variables.label: γ

variables.name: G_T
variables.desc: total irradiance on the tilted plane

variables.name: R_b
variables.desc: beam geometric ratio cos θ / cos θ_z

variables.name: G_bT
variables.desc: beam irradiance on the tilted plane

variables.name: G_dT
variables.desc: sky-diffuse irradiance on the tilted plane

variables.name: G_rT
variables.desc: ground-reflected irradiance on the tilted plane

procedure.python:
def _tilted_irradiance(values):
    """Total irradiance on a tilted plane: isotropic-sky Liu–Jordan model.

    G_T = G_bn·cos θ (beam on the tilted plane) + G_d·(1+cos β)/2 (sky-diffuse view factor)
        + (G_bn·cos θ_z + G_d)·ρ_g·(1−cos β)/2 (ground-reflected, isotropic).
    """
    G_bn, G_d = values['G_bn'], values['G_d']
    rho_g, beta = values['rho_g'], values['beta']
    gamma, phi, delta, omega = values['gamma'], values['phi'], values['delta'], values['omega']
    ctz = math.sin(delta) * math.sin(phi) + math.cos(delta) * math.cos(phi) * math.cos(omega)
    if ctz <= 0:
        raise MechError('sun is below the horizon at this hour angle/latitude/declination '
                        '(cos of the zenith angle <= 0)')
    ct = (math.sin(delta) * math.sin(phi) * math.cos(beta)
          - math.sin(delta) * math.cos(phi) * math.sin(beta) * math.cos(gamma)
          + math.cos(delta) * math.cos(phi) * math.cos(beta) * math.cos(omega)
          + math.cos(delta) * math.sin(phi) * math.sin(beta) * math.cos(gamma) * math.cos(omega)
          + math.cos(delta) * math.sin(beta) * math.sin(gamma) * math.sin(omega))
    warnings = []
    beam_cos = ct
    if ct <= 0:
        beam_cos = 0.0
        warnings.append('beam irradiance set to zero: the tilted surface faces away from the sun '
                        '(cos of the incidence angle <= 0)')
    Rb = beam_cos / ctz
    G_bT = G_bn * beam_cos
    G_dT = G_d * (1.0 + math.cos(beta)) / 2.0
    G_horiz = G_bn * ctz + G_d  # global irradiance on the horizontal
    G_rT = G_horiz * rho_g * (1.0 - math.cos(beta)) / 2.0
    out = {'G_T': G_bT + G_dT + G_rT, 'cos_theta_z': ctz, 'cos_theta': ct, 'R_b': Rb,
           'G_bT': G_bT, 'G_dT': G_dT, 'G_rT': G_rT}
    if warnings:
        out['_warnings'] = warnings
    return out

assumptions: Isotropic sky and ground; beam on the horizontal is G_bn·cos θ_z. Raises an error when the sun is below the horizon (cos θ_z ≤ 0) and zeroes the beam term (with a warning) when the surface faces away from the sun.

renewables.solar_collector.title: Flat-plate collector efficiency (Hottel–Whillier–Bliss)

variables.name: eta
variables.desc: instantaneous collector efficiency (can be negative at night/high ΔT)
variables.label: η

variables.name: Fr_UL
variables.desc: heat-removal factor × overall loss coefficient, F_R U_L

variables.name: G
variables.desc: incident solar irradiance on the collector plane

assumptions: Steady state, F_R(τα) and F_R U_L from collector test data (inputs), no incidence-angle modifier. Uses T_in rather than a mean plate temperature. Q_u and η are signed (night-time or high-ΔT operation loses heat); zero irradiance is rejected because efficiency is undefined there.
method_references: Hottel–Whillier–Bliss collector model, η = F_R(τα) − F_R U_L (T_in − T_amb)/G (recalled)

renewables.pv_power.title: Photovoltaic array power output
assumptions: η is the overall system efficiency at the operating conditions (cell, inverter, wiring, temperature and mismatch losses already folded in).

renewables.pv_derate.title: Photovoltaic efficiency temperature derating

variables.name: eta
variables.desc: module efficiency at the cell temperature
variables.label: η

variables.name: eta_ref
variables.desc: module efficiency at the reference temperature
variables.label: ηref

variables.name: beta_T
variables.desc: temperature coefficient of maximum power (magnitude, e.g. 0.004 /K)

assumptions: Linear derating η = η_ref[1 − β_T(T_c − T_ref)]; β_T is the (positive) magnitude of the power temperature coefficient (enter e.g. 0.004 /K, not −0.004 /K). A cell cooler than T_ref gives η above η_ref.
method_references: Photovoltaic temperature derating, η = η_ref[1 − β_T(T_c − T_ref)] (recalled)

renewables.wind_power_density.title: Wind power density (kinetic-energy flux)

variables.name: p_density
variables.desc: wind power per unit swept area

assumptions: Power in the wind per unit area, ½ρv³. The Betz limit (16/27 of this, for a turbine) is in the turbomachinery section.
method_references: Kinetic-energy flux of a wind stream, P/A = ½ρv³

renewables.geothermal_efficiency.title: Geothermal plant thermal and utilization efficiency

variables.name: Q_in
variables.desc: heat transfer rate from the geofluid

assumptions: Utilization efficiency is referenced to the dead-state temperature of the surroundings; enthalpies are inputs (or take them from the steam calculators). Requires h_in > h_0 and positive Q_in and ṁ.
method_references: Geothermal thermal and utilization efficiency definitions (recalled)

renewables.boiler_efficiency.title: Boiler efficiency by the direct method (steam/feed enthalpies from CoolProp)

variables.name: T_steam
variables.desc: steam outlet temperature (used only when superheated)

assumptions: Direct method on the fuel HHV. Steam and feed enthalpies come from CoolProp (IAPWS-IF97); steam_condition="saturated" uses saturated vapour at P_steam (quality Q = 1) and "superheated" uses the T_steam/P_steam state (rejected if that state is liquid). Errors when h_steam ≤ h_feed or the efficiency would exceed 1.
method_references: Boiler efficiency by the direct method, η = ṁ_s(h_s − h_f)/(ṁ_f·HHV) (recalled)

renewables.steam_generation_rate.title: Steam generation rate from a heat input (enthalpies from CoolProp)

variables.name: Q_in
variables.desc: heat transfer rate into the water/steam

variables.name: T_steam
variables.desc: steam outlet temperature (used only when superheated)

assumptions: Enthalpies from CoolProp (IAPWS-IF97); ṁ_s = Q_in/(h_s − h_f). steam_condition="saturated" uses saturated vapour at P_steam (quality Q = 1), "superheated" the T_steam/P_steam state. Errors when h_steam ≤ h_feed. No blowdown or reheater terms.
method_references: Steam generation rate ṁ = Q/(h_steam − h_feed) (recalled)

renewables.heat_rate.title: Power plant heat rate (energy input per unit electricity out)

variables.name: HR
variables.desc: heat rate as energy in per unit electricity out (1/η; ×3600 → kJ/kWh, ×3412 → Btu/kWh)

variables.name: eta
variables.desc: plant net efficiency (electricity out / heat in)
variables.label: η

assumptions: HR = 1/η is the dimensionless heat rate (J of heat in per J of electricity out). The conventional numbers follow by re-expressing the output unit: 3600/η kJ/kWh or 3412/η Btu/kWh — the unit conversion carries the 3600/3412, not the equation.

renewables.capacity_factor.title: Power plant capacity factor

variables.name: E
variables.desc: actual energy generated over the period

assumptions: Fraction of the rated output actually produced; distinct from availability (which ignores derating and curtailment).
method_references: Capacity factor = energy delivered / (rated power × time) (recalled)

source.derivation: Inverting δ = 0 gives two days, n = 81 (March equinox) and n = 263.5 (September equinox); the solver returns the root closest in log-distance to the example n = 172: |log(263.5/172)| = 0.427 < |log(81/172)| = 0.753, so n = 263.5
2 hours after solar noon: ω = (π/12)(14 − 12) = π/6 = 30°
Equinox noon, south-facing: cosθ = cosδ cosφ cosβ cosω + cosδ sinφ sinβ cosγ cosω = cos(φ − β) = cos(−5°) = 0.996195 → θ = 5°

Afternoon (ω = +30°, sun west of noon) and west-facing (γ = +45°): cosθ = sin20 sin40 cos30 − sin20 cos40 sin30 cos45 + cos20 cos40 cos30 cos30 + cos20 sin40 sin30 cos45 cos30 + cos20 sin30 sin45 sin30 = 0.190414 − 0.089476 + 0.539911 + 0.253632 + 0.094223 = 0.988705 → θ = 8.6199°

Southern hemisphere, SOUTH-facing (pole-facing) panel: γ = 0 means due south in this convention in both hemispheres. Noon: cosθ = cos(φ − β − δ) = cos(−35° − 30° − (−15°)) = cos(−50°) = 0.642788 → θ = 50° (independent ENU sun-vector · panel-normal gives 50.000°). [Relabelled after verify21f: previously described as north-facing]
Horizontal surface at equinox noon: cosθz = cosφ = cos40° = 0.766044; R_b = 1; G_bT = 1000·0.766044 = 766.044; G_dT = 100 (sky view factor (1+1)/2 = 1); ground term (1−cosβ)/2 = 0. G_T = 866.044 W/m²

North-facing wall (γ = 180°, β = 90°) at equinox noon: the surface faces away from the sun, cosθ = −sin40° = −0.642788 ≤ 0, so the beam is clipped to zero. cosθz = cos40° = 0.766044; G_dT = 100(1+cos90°)/2 = 50; ground-reflected = (1000·0.766044 + 100)·0.2·(1−cos90°)/2 = 866.044·0.1 = 86.604; G_T = 0 + 50 + 86.604 = 136.604 W/m²
Cell cooler than reference: T_c − T_ref = −15 K; η = 0.20(1 − 0.004·(−15)) = 0.20·1.06 = 0.212
